newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba hits Spanish Foreign Minister over tourist case.
newsitem.headline: Cuba hits Spanish Foreign Minister over tourist case.

text.p: Cuba on Thursday furiously attacked Spanish Foreign Minister Abel Matutes over remarks he made after a Spanish tourist was prevented from leaving the island following a traffic accident.
Cuban Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina told a news conference Matutes was "a liar, a blackmailer and an interferer."
He added the Spanish minister's comments were "in the worst style of Yankee, now Spanish, arrogance."

Matutes said on Wednesday that Spain would consider issuing an advisory recommending its citizens not travel to Cuba, as well as taking other measures, if the case involving tourist Jesus Martin was not rapidly resolved.
"This situation is intolerable," Matutes told state radio. "Spain is going to use all its resources and those of its European partners to get his immediate release and return to Spain."
The row over Martin, who is still in Cuba pending clearance to leave from police and judicial authorities, is the latest diplomatic spat between Cuba and its former colonial master.

Ties have been tense since the conservative Spanish government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar took office last May, promising a tougher stance on President Fidel Castro's government than its Socialist predecessor.

"This ministry, this nation, this minister, we do not accept lies or blackmail," Robaina said. "For nearly four decades (since the 1959 revolution) our country has shown it does not give in to pressure or blackmail," he added.
Robaina made an unusual appearance at his ministry's regular weekly news briefing to denounce Matutes.
He said he had studied Matutes comments in detail, "so we are not improvising any reply." The Spanish minister's comments were "arrogant, interfering and above all false", Robaina said.
He went through the Spanish minister's version of events concerning the Martin case point by point, saying it was riddled with errors.
Robaina said that contrary to Matutes's version that the accident was not serious, the passenger on a motorcycle that collided with a vehicle driven by Martin sustained serious back injuries.

Robaina said that according to Matutes, Martin had been imprisoned. But in fact the Spanish tourist was never detained, apart from the time at a police station needed to take his statement following the accident, the Cuban minister said.

Martin has been prevented from leaving for home since the accident, which Robaina said occured earlier this month and not last month as Matutes said. The Cuban minister added it was normal for authorities to investigate such an accident.

In brief comments to Reuters television on Wednesday, Martin said he was staying with Cuban friends and was still awaiting permission to leave the country. He said he had still received no clear reply on the case from authorities although he hoped to be able to leave in the next two days.
Spanish consul Eduardo Cerro, commenting on the case to Spanish journalists in Havana on Wednesday, said the Spanish media had overblown the seriousness of the Martin case.
